note: The lead set work to null on 2026-10-31: no text read says New Zealand sets no minimum age for work; Employment NZ's page states rules for workers under 15 and names none, which is silence, not a statement. Majority: null. The Age of Majority Act 1970 on legislation.govt.nz answered with an AWS WAF challenge (HTTP 202, empty body) and was not pursued; archive.org has a snapshot of its whole text (19 November 2025) but every fetch from web.archive.org failed this turn (the tunnel closed mid-exchange), so it wasn't read. Work: Employment New Zealand's 'Hiring young people' page (employment.govt.nz, MBIE, read 2026-10-31) sets out the rules for employing people 19 or under by age band and names no minimum age: employees 17 or under can sign an employment agreement; if the employee is 15 or under a guardian can sign it on their behalf; there is no minimum wage for those 15 or under; school-aged students 15 or under may work only outside school hours (an education requirement, ss. 54 and 240 of the Education and Training Act 2020, unless exempted) and not between 10pm and 6am (Part 4 of the Health and Safety at Work Regulations 2016); those 14 or under may not work in or visit certain workplaces. A search for an official statement in so many words that there is no minimum age found only secondary sources (HR press, law firms, a 2009 academic paper) saying so. The form holds from 0, performers free (my reading: no law sets an age below which a person may not be employed, so a child performer is held only by the hours, school and workplace limits, which the form doesn't hold). Service: null. No conscription law or defence page was read.

sources.title: Hiring young people, Employment New Zealand (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
sources.said: If the employee is 15 years old or under, a guardian can sign the agreement on their behalf. ... If you hire any school-aged students who are 15 years old or under, their work hours must: ... be outside of school hours only (this is an education requirement) ... not be between 10pm and 6am (this is a health and safety requirement).
